prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1383; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On arrival, I found a rear-end collision involving two vehicles at an intersection in League City, Texas. Driver 1 was stopped in the travel lane when the vehicle operated by Driver 2 struck its rear bumper. Driver 2 reported a wrist fracture and was treated at the scene before being transported for further care. Driver 1 said the impact was sudden and that the vehicle was stationary at the time. A Passenger seated in the front right seat of Driver 1's vehicle was also present and corroborated the account. I confirmed that Driver 2 was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Damage to both vehicles is consistent with the described impact, and photographs taken at the scene show the damage locations I observed. I found no earlier damage to either vehicle. No independent witnesses were located. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. Based on my observations, the injury reported by Driver 2 is consistent with a collision of this type.
